dedupe_keys.name: tgrains crop model web application for alternative regional food systems east anglia and south wales

description: An interactive visual tool that makes a mathematical crop model usable by non-specialists, to explore the financial, dietary and ecosystem effects of changing arable crop areas and pastoral grazing in two contrasting UK farming areas, East Anglia and South Wales. The Zenodo record says the web tooling was built in the TGRAINS project by Samantha Mitchell Finnigan and Adrian Clear, the mathematical model by Ryan Sharp and Alice Milne at Rothamsted Research (bundled as a standalone shared library), and that it was used in stakeholder workshops in June 2021. Version 1.0 was published on 4 September 2024 as three downloadable ZIP files, the front end (0.3 MB), the crop model (5.3 MB) and documentation (21 MB), under CC BY 4.0 and MIT. Coverage is the two UK regions. Caveats: the model is a compiled library, so its equations must be read from the documentation. For simulation it shows how land use change shifts regional food output, farm income and nutrition, useful for testing food supply resilience of a region. Related catalogue records include the FABIO food and agriculture biomass input-output tables and the synthetic farm population of North Rhine-Westphalia.
